avoid_supplements.name: Magnesium Supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Magnesium potentiates neuromuscular blockade and prolongs paralysis duration by reducing acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue magnesium supplements at least 24-48 hours before anesthesia; inform anesthesiologist of recent supplementation

avoid_supplements.name: Calcium Channel Blockers (Supplement Form)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Enhanced neuromuscular blockade and prolonged apnea through decreased acetylcholine release and sensitivity
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid supplemental calcium channel blocking agents; coordinate with anesthesiologist if patient taking prescription versions

caution_supplements.name: Potassium Supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Succinylcholine causes transient hyperkalemia; elevated baseline potassium may increase cardiac arrhythmia risk
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum potassium levels; assess risk-benefit in patients requiring supplementation

caution_supplements.name: Corticosteroid Supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May increase potassium release in response to succinylcholine-induced muscle depolarization
caution_supplements.action: Use lowest effective dose; baseline electrolyte monitoring recommended

avoid_foods.name: High-Potassium Foods (Bananas, Spinach, Tomatoes, Potatoes)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Succinylcholine causes acute potassium release from muscles; high dietary potassium elevates baseline levels and increases hyperkalemia risk
avoid_foods.action: Reduce intake of high-potassium foods 24 hours before planned anesthesia; maintain normal dietary potassium otherwise

caution_foods.name: Licorice
caution_foods.mechanism: May cause potassium depletion and electrolyte imbalances that could affect neuromuscular function and cardiac stability during succinylcholine use
caution_foods.action: Limit licorice consumption; ensure adequate electrolyte balance perioperatively

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit
caution_foods.mechanism: May inhibit plasma pseudocholinesterase metabolism slightly, potentially prolonging drug effect marginally
caution_foods.action: Minimal clinical concern; routine dietary restriction not necessary

monitoring_notes: Succinylcholine's primary concern involves potassium release and prolonged blockade in patients with pseudocholinesterase deficiency. Monitor serum potassium, electrolytes, and cardiac rhythm perioperatively, particularly in patients with renal disease, burns, or concurrent medications affecting potassium homeostasis.
